subject: ClarifyHealth POC: environment selection, success criteria, and access onboarding
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@clarifyhealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: ClarifyHealth POC: environment selection, success criteria, and access onboarding

Hi Nora — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery + the concrete next steps so we stay aligned on scope and timeline.

Call summary (what we heard)
- Objective: Validate Redwood inference for patient-summarization workflows (PHI) across batch and streaming traffic.
- Success criteria (customer-side): 1) end-to-end summary accuracy >= baseline on 3 seed prompt sets; 2) 95th percentile latency < 350ms for single-record requests; 3) embeddings similarity +/- 2% vs baseline for reranking; 4) integration validation with their de-id pipeline.

Hosting options we discussed
1) Hosted API (fastest): minimal setup, 24–48 hours to get a sandbox. Pros: quickest path to sample integration and prompt tuning. Cons: less data isolation — may not meet compliance for PHI without additional controls.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved GPU pool): predictable throughput, isolated capacity. Pros: good middle ground for performance testing; can be provisioned in ~5 business days. Cons: requires infra approvals and cost commit.
3) VPC/private trial (recommended if PHI in scope): Redwood control plane with customer-managed VPC, private peering and strict egress rules. Pros: meets strict data controls and network isolation; we can integrate with your IdP for SSO. Timeline: ~8–10 business days to stand up a trial environment assuming your network team can prioritize peering/Firewall allowlist.

Our recommendation
- Given PHI and your compliance posture, we recommend starting with a VPC trial. If you want parallel progress for prompt-level validation, we can open a hosted sandbox for integration tests in parallel (no PHI data) while VPC setup completes.

Immediate next steps / owners (proposed)
- ClarifyHealth: provide primary sysadmin contact for VPC peering and the CIDR ranges to allow. (owner: Nora)
- Redwood infra (Ben Carter): prepare VPC trial runbook, network diagram, and SSO config. (owner: Ben)
- Redwood CSM (Soojin Lee): coordinate evaluation prompts, baseline datasets, and schedule kickoff. (owner: Soojin)
- Redwood AE (me): drive the mutual action plan and dates. (owner: Jonas)

Requested artifacts we will attach/need
- Redwood: SOC2 summary, VPC network template, SSO/SCIM integration guide (attached).
- ClarifyHealth: sample de-id pipeline description, approved CIDR/IPs, and point of contact for Ops.

Proposed timeline (if we start this week)
- Day 0–2: exchange network details, access, and SOC2 docs. Hosted sandbox ready in 24–48h (no PHI).
- Day 3–7: VPC peering work (customer network tasks dependent).
- Day 8–12: validate connectivity, provision trial resources, run initial smoke tests.

Can you confirm: 1) you’re comfortable with us starting hosted sandbox for non-PHI integration in parallel, and 2) the best sysadmin contact we should loop for peering?

Attachments: [Attachment: network-diagram.pdf (PDF)] [Attachment: vpc-sso-setup-guide.pdf (PDF)] [Attachment: soc2-summary.pdf (PDF)]

Thanks — I’ll draft a short mutual action plan after you confirm owners.

— Jonas Weber
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Jonas — this is helpful and aligns with our internal readout. Quick answers:
- We prefer the VPC/private trial given the PHI requirement. We can run non-PHI integration on a hosted sandbox in parallel, yes.
- Sysadmin contact: Samir Khanna (samir.khanna@clarifyhealth.ai), cc’d here on future messages. He handles peering and firewall.
- Timeline: the network team can prioritize if we lock down requirements this week. Please share the SOC2 summary and network template (I see them attached).

A couple of asks from our side:
1) Can you include a short runbook for test data de-identification and recommended test dataset size for accurate perf signals?
2) Do you support cert-based mutual TLS or only IP allowlisting for the VPC trial?

If you can share the answers and the mutual action plan, we’ll aim to target a kickoff the week after next.

— Nora
Head of Infrastructure, ClarifyHealth
Nora.Patel@clarifyhealth.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@clarifyhealth.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-02T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClarifyHealth POC: environment selection, success criteria, and access onboarding

Hi Nora — Ben here (solutions engineering). Quick technical checklist and answers to your questions.

mTLS / Network options
- We support both IP allowlisting and mutual TLS for the VPC trial. For stricter isolation we recommend mTLS + IP allowlist. If your environment prefers certs, we'll exchange CA-signed certs and a short TLS handshake test.

Runbook / required artifacts (what we need from ClarifyHealth)
- CIDR(s) for peering + egress rules to allow Redwood inference subnets (I’ll send the exact CIDRs in a follow-up).
- Firewall rules: allow outbound to 52.210.0.0/16 (example) and inbound for jumpbox if you want support access.
- Point of contact with VPN/peering permissions (Samir).
- For test datasets: 500–1,000 de-identified records is usually sufficient for perf/accuracy signals; if you want statistical confidence for edge cases, 2–3k is better. Redactions: keep PII replaced with placeholders and preserve token distribution.

Estimated effort / timing (subject to ClarifyHealth network availability)
- Hosted sandbox (non-PHI): 24–48 hours to provision.
- Dedicated sandbox: ~5 business days to reserve and provision GPUs.
- VPC trial (peering+mTLS): 8–10 business days (includes cert exchange & networking validation).

Owners at Redwood (for clarity)
- Ben Carter — infra provisioning & network runbook (ben.carter@redwood.ai).
- Soojin Lee — evaluation plan, success criteria execution, test scheduling (soojin.lee@redwood.ai).
- Jonas Weber — commercial lead and MVP acceptance.

Attachments included: network-diagram.pdf, vpc-sso-setup-guide.pdf. I’ll drop the exact allowlist CIDRs in a separate secure note.

Let me know if you want me to schedule a 30-min technical kickoff with your network team (I recommend we include Samir + a network engineer).

— Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
